skill.name: jira-safe
skill.description: Plan and create SAFe-aligned Jira work items with epics, stories, subtasks, acceptance criteria, and parent-child links.
skill.summary: Create SAFe Jira hierarchies and workflow guidance for Jira Cloud projects.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, JavaScript template literals, Jira issue keys, and expected Jira API calls. Confirmed risks remain around the documented bulk delete helper, bulk creation scripts without dry-run safeguards, and Python scripts that load a parent .env file. I found no prompt injection or evidence of third-party credential exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Bulk Jira deletion helper can remove live project data.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the helper from marketplace content, or require dry-run mode, explicit confirmation, issue count preview, and project allowlists before deletion.

remediation.issue: Python scripts load a parent .env file that may contain unrelated secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Read only a skill-local credentials file or require explicit environment variables, and parse only the JIRA_* keys needed by the script.

remediation.issue: Jira API token is sent to the configured base URL without host validation.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and validate that JIRA_BASE_URL belongs to the expected Atlassian Cloud site before attaching Authorization headers.

remediation.issue: Sample scripts can create or transition real Jira issues.
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run option and make production execution require an explicit project key and user confirmation.

semantic_findings.title: Bulk Jira Issue Deletion Helper
semantic_findings.description: The documented bulkDeleteIssues helper searches a project and deletes each issue with deleteSubtasks=true. This can remove live Jira project data if copied or run without strong safeguards.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The function name, DELETE method, loop over issues, and deleteSubtasks=true parameter directly show destructive Jira behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Bulk Jira Issue Creation Without Dry Run
semantic_findings.description: The create-mvp and create-two-level scripts create epics, stories, and subtasks directly after startup. They do not provide a dry-run mode or an interactive confirmation before changing a live Jira project.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both scripts enter main execution and call createIssue loops that post Jira issues with only rate limiting. The behavior is intentional automation, but it can flood production Jira if run by mistake.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent SAFe hierarchy when planning Jira work. This skill drafts epics, stories, subtasks, and Jira API workflows.
actual_capabilities: Provides SAFe templates for epics, features, stories, and subtasks.
Explains Next-Gen and Classic Jira parent-linking differences.
Builds acceptance criteria with Given-When-Then structure.
Includes JavaScript and Python scripts for Jira Cloud issue creation.
Documents Jira workflow transitions, comments, and issue hierarchy patterns.
Shows examples for bulk creation and project issue cleanup.
limitations: Requires Jira Cloud credentials and a valid project key.
Assumes Jira issue types and fields match the documented project patterns.
Scripts can make live Jira changes and should be reviewed before execution.
Does not verify user permissions or custom field configuration automatically.

use_cases.title: Plan Product Backlogs
use_cases.description: Create epics, stories, and subtasks with SAFe language before sprint planning.

use_cases.title: Standardize Engineering Work
use_cases.description: Convert feature ideas into Jira-ready stories with clear acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Automate Jira Setup
use_cases.description: Use the included scripts as references for creating linked Jira issues.

prompt_templates.title: Create a SAFe Story
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SAFe user story for [feature]. Include persona, goal, benefit, and three acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Break Down a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Break [feature name] into Jira stories and subtasks. Use SAFe hierarchy and clear Given-When-Then criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Jira Hierarchy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Jira-ready SAFe hierarchy for [initiative]. Include one epic, linked stories, subtasks, labels, and dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare API Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Jira Cloud workflow for [project key]. Include project type checks, parent linking, transition steps, and safety checks.

output_examples.input: Plan an onboarding epic for a new customer portal.
output_examples.output: An epic summary, business outcome, success metrics, scope, and linked stories for account setup, profile completion, and first login.

output_examples.input: Break a billing feature into implementation stories.
output_examples.output: A feature outline with stories for subscription checkout, payment status, invoices, and cancellation, each with acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: Prepare Jira workflow guidance for a Next-Gen project.
output_examples.output: A concise checklist covering project detection, parent fields, subtask issue type, transitions, comments, and credential requirements.

best_practices: Review generated Jira changes before running any script against production projects.
Use least-privilege Jira API tokens for issue creation and workflow updates.
Confirm project type before choosing parent fields or custom field IDs.
anti_patterns: Running bulk creation or deletion examples without a dry run.
Committing Jira API tokens or environment files to source control.
Using Classic custom fields in a Team-managed Jira project without validation.

faq.question: Does this skill work with Jira Cloud?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples target Jira Cloud REST API v3.

faq.question: Can it support Team-managed projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents the parent field pattern used by Next-Gen Team-managed projects.

faq.question: Does it create issues automatically?
faq.answer: The skill includes scripts that can create issues when users run them with Jira credentials.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: The scripts expect Jira email, Jira API token, base URL, and optionally a project key.

faq.question: Can it generate acceptance criteria?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Given-When-Then examples for stories and subtasks.

faq.question: Should I use it in production Jira projects?
faq.answer: Review every generated action first, especially scripts that create, transition, comment, or delete issues.
